name: Vertebral Compression Fracture
definition: Compression failure of a vertebral body, frequently related to osteoporosis in older adults but also possible with trauma, malignancy or other bone disease.

typical: Pain often worsens with movement or position change
Height loss or kyphotic deformity may develop

redFlags.item: Multiple or recurrent fragility fractures require bone-health assessment

investigations.principle: Determine fracture acuity, stability, neurological involvement and possible pathological cause.
investigations.radiographs: Common first-line demonstration of vertebral height loss/deformity.
investigations.MRI: Useful for marrow edema/acuity, neurological compromise, malignancy or uncertain diagnosis.
investigations.boneHealth: Assess osteoporosis and future-fracture risk, including DXA when clinically appropriate.

amber: Persistent severe pain, instability, neurological compromise or suspected pathological fracture needs specialist evaluation; vertebral augmentation is not an automatic default.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Bhagna-related classical concepts may be relevant to fracture care broadly, but osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture requires modern structural and bone-health classification.

patientEducation.summary: Compression failure of a vertebral body, frequently related to osteoporosis in older adults but also possible with trauma, malignancy or other bone disease.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.
